'Antônio Carlos Jobim', Encyclopaedia Britannica biography, read in full. CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: a Brazilian songwriter, composer and arranger who transformed samba rhythms into the intimate music of bossa nova; he left architecture for music, worked as arranger and as music director of Odeon Records, and recorded 'Chega de Saudade' (1958) with João Gilberto, widely recognized as the first bossa nova single; collaborations with Stan Getz and Frank Sinatra; more than 400 songs including 'The Girl from Ipanema' and 'Wave'; also classical works and film scores. Reference-work summary.

'Antonio Carlos Jobim', jazz.com Jazz Encyclopedia entry, read in full: his classical piano teachers, the Rio group that merged jazz harmony with choro and samba cancao, the 1956 songs for the play Orfeu da Conceicao and the film Black Orpheus, Getz's 1962 Jazz Samba and 1963 Getz/Gilberto, his Verve albums, the 1967 Sinatra album, the more adventurous 1967 album Stone Flower, and the decline of the bossa nova craze. Independent encyclopedia entry; admiring in tone and it also covers family matters, which were not used.

'Antonio Carlos Jobim', JazzStandards.com biography, read in full: musical influences (big bands, West Coast jazz, Debussy, Stravinsky, Chopin, Villa-Lobos), his first recording in 1954, the founding of bossa nova with Vinicius de Moraes and Joao Gilberto, his shift to film scoring when the fad waned, his mid-1980s return to touring and a late collaboration with Sting. Short independent biography.

Songwriters Hall of Fame profile of Antonio Carlos Jobim (1991 inductee), read in full: bossa nova as a distillation of samba, his early big-band influences, the song 'The Girl from Ipanema' with lyricist Vinicius de Moraes, and his own statement crediting Joao Gilberto and Stan Getz with contributions to the music. Admiring institutional profile.

Wikimedia Commons file pages for the Arquivo Nacional (Brazil) photographs of Jobim from the Correio da Manha collection (1965 and 1972) and the Commons rights template used for them, wikitext read, checked for the portrait only; no portrait was adopted.

mastery_orientation.rationale: [src_jobim_britannica, src_jobim_jazzcom, src_jobim_jazzstandards | 1940s-1950s | reference biography + encyclopedia entry + short biography] The sources describe a long classical training with several teachers (including a German piano teacher who introduced Villa-Lobos), study of composition and theory, early work as an arranger and transcriber, and absorption of Debussy, Stravinsky, Chopin and big-band jazz before bossa nova. The training is documented; the sources do not describe his own practice or standards.

adaptability.rationale: [src_jobim_jazzcom, src_jobim_jazzstandards | 1967-1980s | encyclopedia entry + short biography] jazz.com says his 1967 album Stone Flower was darker and more adventurous than his earlier work, and both sources say that when the bossa nova fad faded he turned to scoring Brazilian films before returning to the international scene in the mid-1980s with his own touring group. The changes of direction are documented; whether they were chosen or forced by the market is not stated.
